meta.description: Hazards (tectonic scarps, seismicity, slopes/boulders, regolith, plume, dust, radiation, micrometeoroids, cold), science features/POIs with coordinates and ages, astrobiology / microbial-survival findings, planetary-protection rules, and published multi-criteria site rankings for the lunar south pole.
meta.coordinate_convention: Decimal degrees; latitude south negative; longitude east-positive; lon_east_180 (-180..180) and lon_east_360 (0..360). Where the notes gave only one form the other was computed during conversion (+/-360).
notes: Values copied from research notes of 2026-11-14; not independently validated.

Evidence labels (as in the notes): ESTABLISHED = measured / documented in primary or official sources; MODEL = result of a published simulation, not a measurement; CONTESTED = published but disputed; SPECULATIVE = hypothesis without supporting data. INTERPRETATION / PROPOSAL are used where the notes use them.

Item 'category' values: hazard_scarp, hazard_seismic, hazard_terrain, hazard_regolith, hazard_plume, hazard_dust, hazard_radiation, hazard_micrometeoroid, hazard_thermal, hazard_lighting, science_feature, crater_age, science_objective, geologic_product, astrobiology, planetary_protection, site_ranking.
There is NO evidence of indigenous lunar life. 'Possible bacteria' refers to forward contamination by terrestrial microbes (modelled dormant survival), not detection of lunar organisms.
No rule forbids landing in or near south-polar PSRs; Category IIb (south of 79 S) means documentation, not prohibition.
None of the published rankings is official; NASA has published no site scores.

items.name: de Gerlache lobate thrust scarp
items.notes: Lies within the de Gerlache Rim 2 candidate region. One relocated N9 solution lies within ~24 km of the de Gerlache scarps (source not uniquely determined).

items.name: Shoemaker scarp
items.notes: ~30 km from Nobile Rim 1; a PSR on the Nobile rim within 20 km of the scarp is landslide-susceptible.

items.name: Lobate thrust scarps: counts

properties.mapped_length_scr: ~582 km of lobate scarps mapped in Krasilnikov et al. Zenodo data v1.3

items.caveat: Statistic; no coordinates.

items.name: Modelled shallow moonquake on a polar scarp

properties.shaking: strong-to-moderate to >= ~40 km; moderate-to-light beyond ~50 km
properties.landslide_trigger: ~2.3% of lunar g (1.62 m/s2) for a 1 m slab on >30 deg slopes at low cohesion
properties.susceptible_areas_C_0_1_kPa: large portions of Shackleton interior walls, its NW rim and parts of Connecting Ridge near the rim; interior walls in Nobile Rim 1; a PSR north of de Gerlache Rim 2; a PSR on the Nobile rim within 20 km of the Shoemaker scarp
properties.observational_check: recent boulder falls on Shackleton's wall seen by ShadowCam; no recent regolith landslides observed where predicted (ice-raised cohesion suggested)

items.caveat: Recurrence rate not quantified.

items.name: Planned seismic instruments

properties.LEMS: Artemis III deployed instrument selected Mar 2024: 3-axis short-period + 3-axis broadband, buried; 3 months to 2 years
properties.Farside_Seismic_Suite: Schrodinger basin, >= 4.5 months; status not confirmed

items.evidence: ESTABLISHED (selection); manifesting after the 2026 re-plan unknown

items.name: Mean slopes of major polar craters (20 m baseline)
Boulder populations near sites 001 (Connecting Ridge) and 004 (Shackleton rim)

properties.blocks: ~8 m blocks at the ridge-rim junction (-89.684, -163.261)

items.name: Generic design environment (DSNE): rocks and regolith depth

properties.rock_cover: rocks >~1 m typically ~1% of area but locally 10-20%

items.name: Narrow rims of de Gerlache and Nobile; Connecting Ridge approaches; Malapert relief

properties.statement: Rims of de Gerlache and Nobile are narrow and flanked by slopes unsuited to a stable landing; Connecting Ridge: slopes up to about 20 deg on rim approaches (low-reliability site); Malapert: summit >5,000 m above base, ~3,500 m cliff
Sub-km crater density drops strongly with slope (diffusive mass wasting); 250-500 m craters survive only ~3.5 Gyr even on plains

items.name: Demonstrated polar landing outcomes

properties.IM-2: 6 Mar 2025, Mons Mouton: altimeter failed, struck a plateau, tipped, skidded, came to rest on its side in a ~20 m shadowed crater (~100 K); regolith coated solar panels
properties.IM-1: 22 Feb 2024, -80.13, 1.44: 12 deg slope, broke a leg, ~30 deg tilt
properties.common_cause: altimetry / navigation sensors, not slope or lighting directly (researcher inference)
properties.crewed_lander_concerns: Starship height -> tip-over risk; cryogenic propellants never used on the Moon; only one uncrewed landing test per provider

items.notes: Coordinates are the IM-2 site as given in this note (29.1958; LROC value elsewhere 29.1957).

items.name: PSR surface porosity from LAMP far-UV albedo

properties.porosity: ~70% in PSRs vs ~40% outside (inferred, not measured)

items.name: PSR bearing capacity from boulder tracks (Sargeant et al. 2020)

properties.sample: 13 boulder tracks in shadowed terrain (70-76 deg latitude per one note; 'at/inside south-polar PSRs' per the other)
properties.result: 'somewhat stronger' than highland/mare at 0.28-1.00 m; statistically indistinguishable at 1-2 m; ice in pore space suggested

items.caveat: Numeric kPa values not retrieved. No in-situ geotechnical measurement of PSR regolith exists.

items.name: Slope-stability inputs used for the south pole

properties.isru_unknowns: cohesion 0-100 kPa; friction angle 10-50 deg; particle size 1-1000 um; bulk density 0.5-2.5 g/cm3; compressive strength 1-100 MPa (LWIMS design inputs still unknown)

items.name: Plume-surface interaction (PSI) for large landers

properties.statement: 'Apollo flight experience cannot be extrapolated to upcoming large Human Landing Systems'; subscale hybrid motor tests over regolith simulant; NASA Langley vacuum-chamber tests (BP-1 simulant) continue into 2026; lunar flight PSI data lacking
properties.chandrayaan_3: exhaust removed about 3 cm of regolith
properties.instrumentation: SCALPSS plume cameras on Blue Moon MK1 Endurance

items.caveat: No validated crater-depth or ejecta-range numbers for Starship/Blue Moon found.

items.name: Lander exhaust contaminating polar cold traps (Prem et al. 2020)

properties.result: water-vapour exhaust globally redistributed within hours; 30-40% remained in exosphere/surface after two months; roughly 20% ultimately freezes out near the poles; contamination scales with exhaust mass and proximity to the poles; water is only ~1/3 of typical exhaust
properties.nasem: most contaminants not expected to penetrate more than a few centimetres; mitigations: mission-specific exhaust modelling, characterised exhaust signatures, witness plates, sampling protocols

items.name: Dust lofting and charging

properties.statement: Electrostatic lofting proposed for near-surface (<1 m, Surveyor) and high-altitude (1-100 km, Apollo) observations; Apollo LEAM terminator enhancement discounted (Grun and Horanyi 2011); LADEE/LDEX measured dust well below Apollo-era estimates; 'dynamic fountain' model: grains <0.1 um lofted ~1-100 km at terminator (open question); lighting and plasma environment 'more complex' at the poles

items.caveat: Surface-potential values (kV) not confirmed from a primary source.

items.name: Surface radiation dose (Chang'e-4 LND)

properties.context: far side, solar minimum; likely an upper limit for GCR; design environment: interplanetary GCR/SEP fluxes divided by 2 plus albedo neutrons

items.caveat: Not a polar measurement.

properties.shackleton_like_crater: 20 km simple crater (proxy for 'Artemis Base Camp 004' near the rim): SEP dose reduced >= 40% inside the crater and >= 10% just outside the rim relative to a flat plain (Geant4, Oct 1989 worst-case SEP)
properties.stubbs_2020: 20 km wide, 3 km deep crater cuts net exposure ~40%
properties.habitat_beside_wall: total dose -44.9% at 15 m depth, -10.7% at 5 m depth (PHITS)

properties.secondary: NASA SP-8013 (Apollo era) in SLS-SPEC-159 DSNE; replacement MeMoSeE predicts ejecta flux ~2-3 orders of magnitude lower for particles >1 ug

items.name: Cold and thermal extremes

properties.psr: ~25 K in coldest polar PSRs (record on Hermite, north pole); Haworth coldest areas never exceed ~40 K; Shackleton floor ~88-90 K; PSR interiors down to -248 C; LCROSS site annual average 37 K; PSR floors below -410 F (~28 K) in places
properties.sunlit: illuminated near-rim sites at Shackleton about -50 +/- 10 C; NASA: above 54 C in sunlit areas to -203 C in PSRs
properties.slope_sensitivity: Chandrayaan-3 ChaSTE at 69.37 S: 355 K (+/-0.5) on ~6 deg Sun-facing slope vs ~332 K (+/-1) on flat ground ~1 m away
properties.eclipse_swing: ~5-hour eclipse took a mid-latitude surface from about +40 C to -170 C (press report)
properties.key_parameter: maximum time in shadow; at best sites 20-50% of a normal lunar night

items.caveat: Diviner summer-max / winter-min values for named features not retrieved from a primary source.

properties.statement: Sun never above 7 deg in landing regions; crews cannot avoid Sun in their eyes; no existing requirement guaranteed functional vision moving between sunlight and shadow (NESC recommended one); shadows ~27x object height; deep shadows can hide large obstacles; Apollo 12 crew thought a ~10 deg slope was ~40 deg; Apollo 12 colour TV camera burned out pointed at a 7.5 deg Sun; in driving simulations crews tacked +/-20-30 deg to avoid glare; LIDAR suggested for hazard sensing

items.name: Shackleton crater
items.size: D 21.0 km, depth 4.2 km, floor 6.6 km
items.age: Late Imbrian: rim 3.51 (+0.05/-0.08) Ga (Tye 2015); 3.60/3.69 Ga (Zuber 2012, flat floor/ejecta)
items.science_value: Pole lies on its rim; PSR floor ~88-90 K; rim peaks sunlit ~80-90% of the time; >= 20 km3 impact melt; interior wall ~30 deg; rim blocks likely Shackleton ejecta that may expose SPA-related lithologies

items.name: Shackleton-de Gerlache Connecting Ridge (junction with Shackleton rim)
items.age: Ancient ridge mantled by Shackleton ejecta
items.science_value: 1:8,000 geomorphic map (Icarus 2022, pii S0019103522000835); ~8 m blocks near junction are primary sampling targets; flat spot with line of sight into Shackleton PSR; illumination 92.27-95.65% at 2-10 m, longest darkness 3-5 days

items.name: de Gerlache crater
items.science_value: PSR pocket incl. possible CO2 cold trap; 2022 study of 'slope exposed ice'

items.name: Haworth crater
items.science_value: Large PSR; coldest areas never exceed ~40 K

items.name: Shoemaker crater
items.size: D 50.9 km (52 km in Tye), depth 3.81 km
items.science_value: H ~146 ppm (LP) / 220-245 ppm (LEND interp.); strongest, most uniform LAMP water-band signal of the four; possibly ~5%+ subsurface ice

items.name: Faustini crater
items.science_value: 664 km2 PSR (3rd largest); floor may hold ejecta from Imbrium, Orientale, Schrodinger; radar-bright signal probably rocks (ShadowCam)

items.name: Nobile crater
items.science_value: Former VIPER site on west rim (Mons Mouton side); Griffin Mission One to land near Nobile with Astrolab FLIP rover

items.name: Mons Mouton (formerly Leibnitz Beta)
items.science_value: Near PSRs and extended illumination; IM-2 landed at -84.7906, 29.1958; IM-4 and Chang'e-8 planned for the plateau

items.name: Malapert Massif (Artemis region centre)
items.size: summit >5,000 m above base; ~3,500 m cliff
items.age: 'Thought to be' SPA rim remnant (>4 Ga)
items.science_value: Flat area near 86 S, 0 E is the heart of the candidate region; nearside slope faces Earth
items.caveat: Coordinates approximate ('approx. -86, 0').

items.name: Cabeus crater
items.science_value: LCROSS ground truth (5.6 +/- 2.9 wt% water + other volatiles); impact at -84.6796, -48.7093
items.caveat: Centre conflict: this note uses Wikipedia -84.9, -35.5; USGS Gazetteer list gives -85.33, -42.13 (see psr_and_ice.json).

items.name: Schrodinger basin (context, outside 80 S)
items.science_value: Volcanic vent (Schrodinger G) and lava flows; target of the Farside Seismic Suite

items.name: South Pole-Aitken basin
items.age: Chang'e-6 norite clasts: Pb-Pb 4247 +/- 5 Ma (interpreted as SPA impact, '4.25 Ga'); second event 3873 +/- 8 Ma (tentatively Apollo basin); crater-count model ages ~4.26-4.31 Ga; CE-6 landing site -41.625, -153.978
items.science_value: Artemis sites targeted for PSR volatiles and ancient deposits related to SPA; Mons Mouton 'possibly' and Malapert 'thought to be' SPA rim remnants
items.evidence: ESTABLISHED measurement; attribution to SPA is the authors' interpretation
items.caveat: No basin centre coordinates in notes.

items.name: Southernmost catalogued lunar pit: Schomberger A 1
items.science_value: No listed pit lies poleward of 80 S (next are the Rutherfurd pits near -60.78); catalogue reported as 281 impact-melt, 15 mare, 5 highland pits. Natural-shelter credit should be zero poleward of 80 S (researcher inference).
items.evidence: ESTABLISHED for the catalogue; polar imaging hampered by lighting

items.name: South-polar plains terrain (basin ejecta)
items.science_value: Interpreted as extensive basin ejecta (Nature Communications 2024)

items.name: SPA material fraction at candidate regions (Gracy and Lee)
items.science_value: Connecting Ridge 46% (rank 3 of 13); Peak Near Shackleton 47% (rank 2 of 13)

items.name: Non-ice resources at the south pole
items.science_value: Highland regolith > 40% O by mass, > 75% anorthite, iron-poor, < 2 vol% ilmenite; FeO differences within polar cap <= ~1 wt%; no Th/KREEP concentration; He-3 average ~4 ppb (unknown at pole); nearest bulk chemistry: Chandrayaan-3 APXS at 69.37 S, 32.32 E: Al2O3 26.1 wt%, FeO+MgO 14.4 wt%, Mg# 70; first in-situ sulfur detection (LIBS). Barely discriminates between south-polar sites.
items.evidence: ESTABLISHED (orbital / Apollo-based); no in-situ measurement poleward of ~70 S

items.name: Haworth (Tye et al. 2015)
items.evidence: MODEL age (Neukum chronology; LOLA 20 m DTM; 1-sigma counting errors only)
items.caveat: Pre-Nectarian absolute ages 'particularly uncertain' (no sample calibration beyond ~3.9 Ga). Coordinates from Wikipedia. Lemelin 2021 lists model age 4.18 Ga.

items.name: Shackleton (Tye et al. 2015)
items.caveat: Zuber 2012: 3.60/3.69 Ga; water-ice note: 'crater 3.4-3.7 Ga'. Conflicting values kept.

items.name: PSR host model ages listed by Lemelin et al. 2021
items.formation_model_age_Ga: Shoemaker 4.15; Haworth 4.18; Faustini 4.10; Sverdrup 1 3.80; Cabeus 1 3.50; Wiechert J 3.20; Nobile 2 3.80
items.caveat: Ages for de Gerlache, Nobile crater, Cabeus crater, Malapert, Slater not retrieved elsewhere.

items.name: Artemis III Science Definition Team report (2020): seven objectives

objectives: Understanding the character and origin of lunar polar volatiles
Interpreting the impact history of the Earth-Moon system
Revealing the record of the ancient Sun and our astronomical environment
Observing the universe and the local space environment from a unique location
Conducting experimental science in the lunar environment
properties.site_findings: science return 'intrinsically linked' to landing site; proximity to SPA and PSR units key; diverse samples incl. subsurface and volatile-bearing in sealed containers; pre-positioned assets and mobility recommended
properties.sample_mass: NASA requirement at least 35 kg, goal 100 kg; SDT scenarios 25 kg and 83 kg; Apollo average 64 kg; LEAG recommended >= 150 kg (sources differ on 'the' target)

items.evidence: ESTABLISHED (via faithful secondary list; report PDF not opened)

items.name: Published geologic maps and site studies

properties.Krasilnikov_2023_Icarus_394_115422: 1:300,000 map of south circumpolar region; model ages for ~200 units; ArcGIS data on Zenodo
properties.Krasilnikov_2023_SSR: modelled ejecta-thickness maps 70 S to pole
properties.Krasilnikov_2024_Icarus_420_116190: stratigraphic cross-sections and provenance at Artemis candidate sites, to 'support a ranking of sites' (ranking details not retrieved)
properties.Boazman_2022_PSJ_3_275: boulder / rocky crater / outcrop maps around sites 001 and 004
properties.PGDA_78: 5 m/pixel LOLA DEMs, slope and uncertainty maps for named sites

items.evidence: ESTABLISHED (publications exist); numerical content largely not retrieved

items.name: Indigenous life detected on the Moon?
items.finding: No. Apollo 11, 12, 14 quarantine/biohazard testing 'revealed no evidence of life or hazard'; quarantine discontinued after Apollo 14.
items.evidence: ESTABLISHED (no detection in any returned sample)

items.name: Conditions for microbial growth/replication on the Moon?
items.finding: No ('no evidence the Moon has liquid water or other ingredients needed for microbial growth and replication'); 'survival' in the 2026 study explicitly excludes growth/reproduction.

items.name: Surveyor 3 / Streptococcus mitis survival claim
items.finding: Almost certainly not survival; Rummel, Allton and Morrison (2011) concluded the team 'only detected their own contamination' (1970 lab handling).
items.evidence: CONTESTED historically, now regarded as refuted

items.name: Organics in Apollo samples and on hardware
items.finding: Amino acids in Apollo regolith (up to ~70 ppb) are 'primarily terrestrial' contamination with minor meteoritic contribution; Apollo hardware cleaned to 10-140 ng/cm2 organic contamination.

items.name: Apollo human-waste bags
items.finding: 96 bags left at six near-equatorial sites; survival 'highly improbable' (Schuerger); no funded retrieval mission found.

items.name: Beresheet tardigrades (2019)
items.finding: Survival unlikely: lab survival up to ~0.9 km/s (825-900 m/s), death above ~1.14 GPa shock; crash shock 'well above' that.

items.name: Chang'e-4 biosphere experiment (2019)
items.finding: Cotton seeds sprouted inside a sealed, pressurised, lit, watered canister; died at first lunar night (canister cooled to about -52 C and lower). Not growth in the lunar environment.

items.name: Schuerger et al. 2019 Lunar Microbial Survival model (sunlit surface)
items.finding: Sunlit external surfaces >100 C, up to 140 C at local noon; ~ -6 logs per 8 h at local noon; vacuum alone ~ -2 logs per 2107 days; deep internal surfaces ~ -0.02 logs per lunation; external surfaces unlikely to retain viable spores after one lunation.

items.name: Moores et al. 2025 (York Univ.): spore survival inside PSRs
items.finding: Bacillus subtilis-type spores: reduction rates -0.0815 (Shackleton) and -0.0683 (Faustini) logs per lunation -> 30.0 yr and 30.8 yr to reach one Sterility Assurance Level (-12 logs); UV dominates for ~4-5 yr, vacuum thereafter; PSRs 'one of the least biocidal environments in the solar system'.
items.caveat: The Shackleton/Faustini result is from Moores et al. 2025, NOT Saxena et al. (correction recorded in the notes).

items.name: Saxena et al. 2026 (NASA Goddard/JSC, Science Advances, DOI 10.1126/sciadv.aec0811)
items.finding: 'Survival' = alive >= 1 Earth day, not growth; Aspergillus niger most UV-resistant, max >= 7 days under optimal conditions; organisms: A. niger, Bacillus subtilis, Staphylococcus aureus, Deinococcus radiodurans, Fusarium spp.; survivable niches range from a miles-wide crater floor to an astronaut boot print; robotic spacecraft can be baked >400 F (~204 C), crews cannot.
items.locations: Nobile Rim, Connecting Ridge, de Gerlache Rim (Artemis candidate regions)
items.evidence: MODEL (paper itself not retrieved; NASA release and news summary)

items.name: NASEM 2020 and NASA OPP on organismal contamination
items.finding: NASEM judged organismal contamination the least concerning for lunar science; any organisms detected would very likely have come from Earth. NASA OPP: 'Crewed missions and biological payloads are not a concern for PP compliance' for the Moon.

items.name: 'Earth's attic' (terrestrial meteorites on the Moon)
items.finding: Armstrong et al. 2002: median surface abundance of terrestrial material ~7 ppm (~20,000 kg per 10 x 10 km). Bellucci et al. 2019: felsic clast in Apollo 14 breccia interpreted as Hadean terrestrial rock.
items.evidence: MODEL (7 ppm); CONTESTED (Apollo 14 clast); polar preservation bonus SPECULATIVE

items.name: Prebiotic / organic interest of PSRs
items.finding: 'No ground-truth chemical analyses of PSR materials or volatiles, at the surface or at depth, currently exist'; LCROSS found light hydrocarbons, sulphur species, ammonia, CO2 consistent with cometary/asteroidal delivery; Haworth/Shoemaker/Faustini floors have ~3.5 Ga retention ages so early ice was likely not preserved at the present surface.

items.name: Lunar Category II (orbiters, flybys)
items.rule: Volatiles-release report not required; organic inventory not required; no bioburden control

items.name: Lunar Category IIa (landing, not in 'a PSR and the lunar poles')
items.rule: Report volatiles released by propulsion/ACS: required; whole-spacecraft organic inventory: not required; no bioburden control. Covers ~99% of the lunar surface.

items.name: Lunar Category IIb (landing or surface operations within a PSR and the lunar poles)
items.rule: Defined as locations south of 79 S latitude and north of 86 N latitude. Volatile release assessment required (4.3.3, pre-launch; 4.3.10, end of mission); full organic inventory required - all organic materials > 1.0 kg (4.3.5); excluded from bioburden management (4.4.1) and cleanroom-assembly requirement (4.4.2). 'No limits on the types or quantities of organics'. Orbiters need the inventory if > 1e-3 probability of landing in a IIb region within 15 years. Return category V (unrestricted).
items.caveat: COSPAR policy texts themselves (2021, 2024, SRT 224 of 2025/2026) could not be opened; whether SRT 224 changed any lunar clause is unverified.

items.name: Timeline of lunar planetary-protection documents
items.rule: 1983 COSPAR Moon Category I; 2008 raised to Category II (polar volatile deposits >= 70 N and S); Jul 2020 NASA NID 8715.128 (Category I-L / II-L: PSRs south of 79 S and north of 86 N, and Apollo/historic sites; expired 9 Jul 2021); 3 Jun 2021 COSPAR IIa/IIb introduced; 24 Sep 2021 NASA NPR 8715.24 (expires 22 Sep 2032); 30 Aug 2022 NASA-STD-8719.27; 27-28 Feb 2024 Organic Inventory Workshop; 20 Mar 2024 COSPAR policy editorial update (SRT 220); 29 May 2025 NASA lunar reporting forms; Nov 2025 / Jan 2026 new COSPAR policy version (SRT 224). NPR 8715.24 'being expanded to include crewed' missions.

items.name: Artemis Accords: safety zones (Sec. 11) and heritage (Sec. 9)
items.rule: Safety zones whose size, scope and duration reflect the nature of operations and 'will be temporary'; preserve 'historically significant human or robotic landing sites, artifacts, spacecraft, and other evidence of activity'. No agreed numerical safety-zone radius.
items.evidence: ESTABLISHED (text); tension with non-appropriation noted by legal scholars

items.name: Proposed protected scientific sites (IAU WG, SESIs, ITU-R RA.479)
items.rule: IAU Working Group on astronomy from the Moon (authorised 15 Sep 2023); 'Sites of Extraordinary Scientific Importance' proposed for the far-side radio-quiet zone and polar cold traps; ITU-R RA.479: far-side shielded zone. 2020 LSSW session suggested pairing similar PSRs (one for science, one for resource use) rather than fixed keep-out zones.
items.caveat: No published rule on minimum stand-off distance from PSRs.

items.name: NASEM 2020, Planetary Protection for the Study of Lunar Volatiles
items.rule: Finding 6: no clear prioritised science objectives for PSRs exist; organic volatiles from landings and habitat venting are the most likely confounders; most combustion products are not organic molecules.

items.name: Pena-Asensio, Neira-Acosta and Sanchez-Lozano 2024 (arXiv:2406.19863; accepted in Acta Astronautica)
items.method: GIS + TOPSIS (cross-checked with MABAC, CoCoSo, VIKOR); 1,247 candidate points in 13 Artemis regions + Site 004, pre-filtered to slope 0-5 deg with 100 m buffer
criteria: C1 total visibility (km2 seen from 40 m HLS window height)
C2 % of 2 km walkable radius with lander line-of-sight
C3 mean illumination x % PSR within 2 km
C5 number of geologic units within 2 km (USGS 1:5M map)
C6 mafic abundance (M3 1 um band depth)
items.weights: Baseline: equal weights. Sensitivity: C3 and C4 at 40% each, others 5% each
items.inputs: LOLA DEM/slope 5 m/px (~90% interpolated); illumination/PSR/Earth-shine maps 240 m/px; M3 1.4 km/px
items.result: Top 9 points all in DM2; top-100 share: DM2 36%, Malapert Massif (Site23) 30%, Amundsen Rim (DM1) 13%; no top-100 points in Connecting Ridge Extension (SL3), Leibnitz Beta Plateau (Site20) or Haworth.
items.caveat: Sensitive to the 0-5 deg pre-filter and number of points per region.

items.name: Lemelin et al. 2014 (Planet. Space Sci. 101:149-161)
items.method: GIS multi-parameter overlay, equally weighted stack; six criteria
criteria: (as summarised) volatile-relevant datasets incl. hydrogen, temperature, PSR, slope
items.top_sites: South-polar sites meeting all six criteria: Shoemaker and Faustini; relaxing one adds Haworth, de Gerlache, Cabeus; case study Amundsen (5 north-polar and 7 south-polar regions in total)
items.caveat: Exact six criteria and thresholds not retrieved from primary text. EPSC2020-619 notes these sites lie only inside PSRs and fail rover-accessibility requirements (https://meetingorganizer.copernicus.org/EPSC2020/EPSC2020-619.html).

items.name: Lemelin, LEAG 2016 regions-of-interest update
criteria: PSR within 1 km of lit terrain
items.top_sites: Cabeus, Shoemaker/Nobile, and (north) Peary; adding Earth visibility and lighting makes Peary more favourable than south-polar sites
items.evidence: from a search summary of the presentation
items.caveat: LEAG PDF returned HTTP 403.

items.name: Lemelin et al. 2021 (PSJ) framework
items.method: 169 ice-bearing PSRs scored for abundance / lateral / vertical distribution / fastest sample
items.top_sites: 11 high-priority PSRs: Shoemaker, Haworth, Faustini, Sverdrup 1, Cabeus 1, Wiechert J, Malapert, Nobile 2, PSR 120, PSR 89, PSR 57 (Shackleton not recommended); traverse case studies PSR 89 (20-50 km), Sverdrup 1 (~100 km), Cabeus (~300 km)
items.caveat: Criteria list here is a paraphrase of the table columns in the notes.

items.name: Flahaut et al. 2020 (Planet. Space Sci. 180:104750)
items.method: GIS ROI identification, lander and rover scenarios
criteria: surface ice stable under present thermal regime
supporting UV/VNIR albedo and radar CPR indicators
items.top_sites: 11 ROIs: one broad area >200 x 200 km at the South Pole plus smaller regions near Cabeus, Amundsen, Ibn Bajja, Wiechert J, Idel'son
items.caveat: ROI coordinates and numerical thresholds not retrieved.

items.name: Brown et al. 2022 (Icarus 377:114874)
items.method: Relative ranking of large PSRs from 10 datasets / 8 instruments
criteria: Consistency of ice indicators across datasets (blue/green/orange classes)
items.top_sites: Faustini, Cabeus, de Gerlache, Shoemaker, Haworth, Sverdrup, Slater, Amundsen (Faustini potentially top; Cabeus has direct evidence)
items.caveat: Per-PSR ranking table not retrieved.

items.name: Wueller et al. 2026 (JGR Planets 131, e2025JE009434)
items.method: Illumination + simultaneous Sun/Earth visibility per Artemis candidate region for each midsummer 2025-2032
items.top_sites: 130 candidate landing sites; largest suitable fractional area: Slater Plain, then Nobile Rim 2, Faustini Rim A; smallest: Connecting Ridge Extension, de Gerlache Rim 1, MMA, PCB
items.caveat: Table A1 (130 sites) not retrievable.

items.name: NASA Cross Agency Site Selection Analysis (official)
items.method: Not a published score; constraint-based down-selection

items.name: Other ranking inputs (Krasilnikov 2024; Boazman 2022; Coyan 2025; Cannon and Britt 2020 IFI)
items.method: Geological cross-sections/provenance; accessibility mapping on <15 deg slopes; prospectivity model for Mons Mouton (classes highly prospective / favourable / permissive / non-prospective); Ice Favorability Index (unitless, USGS raster 591 m/px)
items.top_sites: not rankings of named landing sites
